property_summary: For every call to fallback with any msg.value, the reference contract only accepts the call (does not revert) iff msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant instead accepts calls with 5 ether, so there exist inputs where the reference rejects but the mutant accepts (or vice versa).

For any caller and any amount, calling C's fallback succeeds (does not revert) if and only if msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant requiring 5 ether instead will accept some calls (e.g. with 5 ether) that the reference rejects, so the rule 'fallback succeeds exactly for value == 10 ether' is satisfied by the reference for all inputs and broken by the mutant for some input.

The reference contract accepts (fallback call succeeds) if and only if msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant instead accepts when msg.value == 5 ether, so there exist fuzzed msg.value inputs where the reference reverts but the mutant does not.

For every caller and every wei amount, calling C's fallback succeeds (does not revert) exactly when msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant changes that acceptance condition to 5 ether, so there exist fuzzed amounts where the reference reverts but the mutant accepts (or vice versa).

For every caller and amount, C's fallback only accepts (does not revert) when msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant changes the required value to 5 ether, so there exist fuzzed amounts where the reference reverts but the mutant accepts.

For any call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether, contract C always updates pastBlockTime only when block.timestamp strictly increases (i.e., fallback either reverts if timestamp is not greater or leaves pastBlockTime unchanged); the mutant that removes the time check can update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, contract C only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than its previous value; the mutant that removes the time check can update pastBlockTime even when timestamp is not greater, so there exist inputs (a sequence of calls with non-increasing timestamp) that make the mutant change pastBlockTime while the reference does not.

For any payable call to fallback with exactly 10 ether, the reference contract only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than its stored value; the mutant that removed the time check can update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, so there exist inputs (a call made at a non-increasing timestamp) where the mutant's pastBlockTime changes but the reference's does not.

For any caller and block.timestamp, when fallback is invoked with exactly 10 ether the reference C either reverts if block.timestamp is not strictly greater than pastBlockTime or else updates pastBlockTime to block.timestamp; the mutant that removed the time check can update pastBlockTime even when timestamp is not greater, so there exist inputs (a call at a non-increasing timestamp) where the mutant changes pastBlockTime but the reference does not.

For any payable call to fallback with msg.value == 10 ether, the reference contract only updates pastBlockTime when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the stored pastBlockTime; the mutant that removed the time check can update pastBlockTime even when block.timestamp is not greater, so there exist inputs (a call when block.timestamp is <= prior pastBlockTime) that make the mutant change pastBlockTime while the reference does not.

After any successful payable call to fallback sending exactly 10 ether from any externally owned caller at a given timestamp, the stored pastBlockTime equals the block.timestamp used in that call (reference preserves timestamp), whereas the mutant sometimes stores block.number instead and thus can make pastBlockTime != block.timestamp.

For any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether and a strictly increasing block.timestamp, the contract's balance becomes 0 whenever the block.number is divisible by 15 (the reference pays out); the mutant that removes the conditional transfer can leave a non-zero balance for some such inputs, so the rule is violated for those inputs.

General rule: If fallback is called with exactly 10 ether and block.timestamp strictly increases, then the contract only transfers its balance to the caller when block.number % 15 == 0; the mutant inverts that condition and will transfer when block.number % 15 != 0, so there exist block numbers where behavior differs.

For any call to fallback with exactly 10 ether and strictly increasing block.timestamp, the original contract transfers its entire balance to the caller iff block.number % 15 == 0; the mutant inverts that check and thus will transfer on some block numbers where the original does not (and vice versa).
